about: Claims of the Scoring Sources lesson. status: verified = the source read it at a file or document ([V] in Addendum D); ours = our own protocol rule, count or run outcome ([C] in Addendum D, run results in the Stage A log, registry EXP-037); inferred = an inference the source marks [I]. Every claim is cited on the page.

claims.text: One score source per key, never mixed by arm.
S1 is the same int8 ONNX job on Kaggle CPU, sharded. It keeps continuity with the earlier tuning only if reproducibility is shown.

S1 pins the settings of the job that made the inherited scores: the same int8 model file and tokenizer, onnxruntime 1.31.0, the CPU execution provider only, 4 threads, memory arena off, one pair at a time with no padding, truncation at 512 tokens, score = sigmoid of the single logit.
ONNX Runtime states that int8 quantized results can depend on the CPU instruction set.
The inherited kernels did not record their CPU instruction-set flags (AVX2, AVX-512, VNNI); the new kernels record them.
Each new kernel first re-scores a fixed seeded sample of 200 inherited keys. Any score that is not bit-equal stops that kernel before it scores new pairs.
S1 stays if and only if every S1 kernel's 200-key check is bit-equal on all 200 keys. Any single mismatch on any kernel selects S2. There is no retry on another kernel.
Exact equality is a defensible stop rule, not a shown feasibility. 200 equal keys support reproducibility; they do not prove equality on unseen keys.
S2 is one GPU job on Kaggle with the bge-reranker-v2-m3 checkpoint at a pinned revision, fp32. All keys are re-scored, including the inherited 15,443 and R's pairs.
Throughput, cost and wall-clock time are not criteria. If S1 is too slow, the job waits; it does not switch.
The switch is decided and recorded before any new score is merged and before any tuning. On a switch, S1 scores from earlier passing kernels are discarded, not merged.
The three inherited score files overlap with 15,443 union keys and 0 conflicting duplicates.
181.6k new pairs at 0.5 pairs/s is about 100 kernel-hours. This is an extrapolation, not a demonstration.
The collector wrote 195,471 unique keys: 13,841 inherited and 181,630 new. Dev 18 items: 81,954 widest-walk pairs; pilot 30: 118,691.
The overlap sample is 200 keys drawn with a fixed seed from the frame of 10,622 inherited keys with known pair text, bound in stage 1.
The probe kernel (Intel Xeon 2.20 GHz) matched 200/200 bit-equal and scored 1,000/1,000 pairs at 0.632 pairs/s.

All 24 shards and the probe were verified: every kernel was bit-equal on the 200-key overlap. CPUs: Intel Xeon 2.20 GHz and AMD EPYC 7B12. Measured 0.52-0.66 pairs/s. 25/25 kernels verified with an overlap result.
Switch: S1. The switch record was committed before the merge.
The merged file holds 197,073 keys (15,443 inherited + 181,630 new); coverage of the collected list 195,471/195,471; 0 conflicting duplicates.

Stage 2 hashes the collected pair list and the merged score file and stores a 100 % coverage report. It is committed before dev_tune runs, and dev_tune refuses a score file whose hash differs from stage 2.

A Mac (ARM) re-score of 50 pairs of the overlap sample gave Spearman 0.987 with the inherited scores but bit-equal 0/50, max |Δ| 0.104. It is a diagnostic of the int8 instruction-set dependence only and does not enter the switch rule.
44/50 sampled pairs reach the 512-token cap. The cap is the same for every arm and frozen in both specifications; its effect on ranking is not measured.
A frozen shared-baseline comparison stays valid under either option.
Dev re-tuning (H only) read the stage-2 score file; the tie rule picked s7-b/2 with k_graph 30. I4 (config 7cae3a31) binds stage 2 and the winner.
Kaggle CPU sessions and concurrency limit the wall-clock time.
Per-item rows and retrieval traces go to a sealed directory; the visible output holds aggregates and the winner only.
The balanced rank rule needs a CE score for every permitted passage at hops 0-2, with no pre-cap; the pair set is the widest walk.
The rank rule takes each hop's best passages by CE score, so a changed score can change which passages fill the slots.
